evals.expected_output: Edits a sops-encrypted file through sops and verifies it still decrypts and carries the right recipients; routes the render and fleet-config repo classes correctly.
evals.prompt: I need to change a secret value in machines/secrets/telsha.enc.yaml — what's the right way to edit it so the file stays valid and the target host can still read it?
assertions: YAML frontmatter parses and 'name' equals 'sks-sops-secrets-authoring'
Frontmatter description starts with 'Use when' and is at most 200 characters
Frontmatter license field is 'Apache-2.0'
Body contains at least one '##' heading
Body states repo-enforced hooks/formatters must not touch .enc files
Body shows a 'sops' edit path (sops <file> or -e/-d pipeline), not a plain-editor edit of the .enc file
Body requires verifying the file still decrypts after the edit with sops --decrypt
Body checks the sops recipient set (sops_age / sops_pgp / sops_kms) after editing
Body treats .enc.env and .enc.conf files as distinct from .enc.yaml and warns against editing them like YAML
Body mentions sops-nix plumbing: sops.defaultSopsFile per host and sops.templates.*
Body delegates manifests-specific detail (recipient keys, devenv wrapper trap, INI store, formatForPath) to its own references/sops-manifests.md

evals.expected_output: Refuses to commit a plaintext secret file and instead edits through sops; flags nix fmt as a corruption risk on .enc files.
evals.prompt: I decrypted telsha.enc.yaml to a plaintext file on disk, edited it in my editor, and now I want to commit the plaintext version and delete the .enc.yaml. Fix my plan.
assertions: YAML frontmatter parses and 'name' equals 'sks-sops-secrets-authoring'
Frontmatter description starts with 'Use when' and is at most 200 characters
Frontmatter license field is 'Apache-2.0'
Body contains at least one '##' heading
Body states that editing a plaintext copy and committing it is wrong, and that edits must go through sops so only the encrypted file is on disk
Body states nix fmt / treefmt must not be run across secrets/*.enc.* and would corrupt the file
Body mentions verifying no accidental plaintext secret is on disk (git status --porcelain secrets/)
Body states deleting the .enc.yaml is not the right move; the encrypted file is the artifact to keep

evals.expected_output: Adds a recipient safely and warns that removing a recipient from a file still consumed by a live host is an availability bug; for manifests uses the three fleet age recipients and the unwrapped sops binary.
evals.prompt: A new operator needs to read the shared machine.enc.yaml. How do I give them access without breaking the hosts that already consume it?
assertions: YAML frontmatter parses and 'name' equals 'sks-sops-secrets-authoring'
Frontmatter description starts with 'Use when' and is at most 200 characters
Frontmatter license field is 'Apache-2.0'
Body contains at least one '##' heading
Body says adding a recipient is the safe direction and the new recipient set must be a superset for every live consumer
Body warns that removing a recipient from a file still in use by another host is an availability bug, not cleanup
Body mentions age recipients (AGE-SECRET-KEY public keys / sops_age metadata) as the mechanism
Body checks the recipient set after the edit with sops and grep on sops_age or sops_*
Body distinguishes the fleet-config per-host recipient model from the render multi-fleet-recipient model
